title: 2005 Royal Air Force Hercules shootdown
summary: RAF Hercules XV179 was shot down by Sunni insurgents in Iraq six minutes after departure from Baghdad. All 10 personnel perished. The Board of Inquiry identified the lack of a fire-suppressant system as a contributory factor, and the right wing was found separated from the fuselage.
probable_cause: Aircraft became uncontrollable after hostile ground-to-air fire caused explosive separation of the outboard right-hand wing. The lack of a fuel tank inerting system in the wing fuel tanks left the aircraft vulnerable to explosive fuel/air mixture development (p. 2-3)

factors.evidence: Aircraft shot down by hostile ground-to-air fire causing explosive wing separation (p. 2-3)
Distress message from crew at 1330Z indicated "We are on fire, we are on fire" after hostile fire impact (p. 2-3)
Right wing outboard section separated explosively from fuselage due to hostile ground-to-air fire impact (p. 2)
All 10 personnel on board were killed - crash was not survivable (p. 2-3)

events.text: RAF Hercules XV179 took off from Baghdad at 1324Z en route to Balad at low level
Aircraft heading north at low level, utilizing low-level flying tactic to mitigate risk from hostile ground-to-air threats (p. 3)
Royal Signals signaller reported fire on board: "No duff, no duff, We are on fire, we are on fire" (p. 2)
Distress message received at 1330Z from crew indicating aircraft on fire (p. 3)
Crash site located by US Apache helicopter crew at 1415Z in hostile area (p. 3)
Wreckage found in two separate locations indicating separation during flight (p. 2)
Right wing found separated from fuselage - outboard right-hand wing explosive separation due to hostile ground-to-air fire (p. 2)

notes: Hostile act clearly established - ground-to-air missile
Fire on board reported by crew
Tactical considerations and system recommendations extracted
auto-repair: cvr was null; dissent was null; related was null

safety_changes: C130 tactics reviewed - low level flying in daylight no longer authorized unless operationally essential (p. 4)
Fuel tank inerting system being investigated for C130 aircraft (p. 4)
Ground-to-air fire reporting and dissemination system improved and procedures reviewed (p. 4)
Air Component Headquarters adapted intelligence procedures and processes for ground-to-air threat reporting (p. 4)

recommendations.text: Review C130 low-level flying tactics to mitigate risk from hostile ground-to-air fire in daylight operations
Consider fitting fuel tank inerting system in C130 aircraft wing fuel tanks to prevent explosive fuel/air mixtures
Improve in-theatre ground-to-air intelligence process and reporting procedures
